newsitem.title: THAILAND: Sino-Thai sees big 1996 profit fall.
newsitem.headline: Sino-Thai sees big 1996 profit fall.

text.p: Thai construction firm Sino-Thai Engineering and Construction Plc's profit is expected to fall sharply this year due to the high interest rate payments on its convertible debentures, a company official said on Monday.
"The company's net profit this year is expected to be about 50 percent lower than last year," the company's managing director Anuthin Chanvirakul told reporters.
In 1995, the company posted a net profit of 369.15 million (US$14.8 million) baht versus 330.52 million in 1994.
"Late this year, the company will have to pay interest on about 300 million baht for existing euro convertible debentures," Anuthin said.
Sino-Thai early this month signed $80 million in syndicated loans with 19 foreign banks in reserve for the redemption of its euro convertible debentures, he said.
The lead arranger for the loan was HSBC Investment Bank Asia.
Sino-Thai in 1993 issued $80 million euro convertible debentures with a 10-year maturity but with a put option at the end of the third year.
